name: Tree topper (makes 1): 22" burlap bow, two upswept loops and two 14" tails, 6" natural jute with 3" black felt paws, wired edges
look: Large topper bow in natural/cream burlap or linen with scattered black paw prints, four loops plus tails. Needs paw-print burlap wired ribbon at least 2.5 in wide (4 in better).
notes: The board's bow: natural burlap about 6" wide, two big upswept loops over shorter tails, black paws about half the ribbon's width. No paw-print burlap is sold at this width, so we glue on 3" felt paws; floral wire glued along the back edges lets the unwired jute hold its shape like the board. Vendor: the 6" jute (B0DQ4BXYKZ) is sold by xingwanworks (18 ratings) and shipped by Amazon from outside Canada, $6.43, Nov 22; the 4" wired burlap (B0CHMLF3NP, Nov 20) is the fallback. The jute is not wired, so the glued edge wire is essential.
how: Cut list from the 6" jute (12 yd roll): one 78" bow strip and one 8" knot piece (2.4 yd with the notches). Work on the drop sheet. (1) Edge wire: on the back face, hot-glue a 79" length of floral wire 1/4" in from each long edge, folding the last 1/2" of wire back at each end so it cannot poke out. The jute is not wired, so this is what holds the loops. (2) Paws, front face only: trace 24 paws on the black felt with the 3" template (page 3) and the white fabric marker (or tape the paper paw to the felt and cut round it). Each paw is 5 pieces: a pad and four toes. Glue 23 on the front face of the strip with fabric glue, alternating left and right of the centre line about every 3.4", none in the middle 4" where the bow is pinched; glue the 24th in the middle of the knot piece. Dry flat overnight. (3) Fray stop: the long edges are hemmed; run a thin bead of fabric glue across the cut ends of the strip and the knot piece. (4) Tie, paws facing you: leave a 14" tail, make a 10" loop to the left (about 22" of ribbon) and a 10" loop to the right, angling both loops up about 20 degrees, and pinch the centre with an 18" piece of floral wire; the second 14" tail hangs down. Fold the knot piece lengthwise in half (3" wide, paw out), wrap it round the pinch and hot-glue it at the back. V-notch both tails 1" deep and seal the notch with fabric glue. (5) Fix: zip-tie it to the top stem with two of the organizers' zip ties and twist the 18" wire ends round the stem (two more 18" wires if it leans). Shape the loops up and round and let the tails hang about 25 degrees off vertical, like the board: about 22" across with 14" tails.
tools: Zip ties (2, supplied with the tree)

name: Golden retriever plush, sitting, 12" (Wild Republic Cuddlekins)
look: Seated golden-retriever PUPPY figurine ornament, front-facing, soft resin look, about 3-4 in, with a red-and-green tartan scarf knotted at the neck.
notes: Wild Republic Cuddlekins 12" (about 11" tall sitting). A paler, peachier gold than the board's honey-gold puppy, and its grey felt paw pads face forward: wire it tilted back with the hind feet tucked onto the branch so the pads face down, and drape the scarf ends over the front paws. Wired round the body to the trunk under its tartan scarf. Amazon.ca seller, 4.4 stars (47), $19.37, Nov 17-20.
how: Each dog (about 100 g): fold a 72" floral wire in half, wrap the doubled wire round the belly under the scarf and twist both ends round a main branch near the trunk; add one of the organizers' zip ties round the body and branch, since the tree is moved several times. Sit it tilted back with the hind feet tucked onto the branch so the grey pads face down, and drape the scarf ends over the front paws. Under the tree, the dog and the cat sit side by side by the basket, wired to each other and to the basket handle with two 18" floral wires hidden under the scarves.

name: Grey tabby kitten plush, 9" long x 6" tall, crouching (Aurora Miyoni Tots)
look: Strongly striped grey-brown tabby with a white chest, muzzle and paws, in a fringed tartan scarf.
notes: The board's coat: strong grey-brown mackerel stripes with a white chest, muzzle and paws. It crouches (front paws forward, head up) where the board's cats sit upright, so it lies along a branch on the tree. Snip off the gold Miyoni tag; the scarf covers the spot. Sold by Amazon US (cross-border, no import fee shown), 4.8 stars from 2,170 ratings, free delivery Nov 20, but only 8 left on Nov 16: order it first.
how: Each cat (about 136 g): snip off the gold Miyoni tag. Fold a 48" floral wire in half, wrap the doubled wire round the body behind the front legs, under the scarf, and twist both ends round a sturdy branch so the cat lies along it, face out. Under the tree it sits beside the dog (see the golden retriever).

name: Doghouse ornaments (makes 6): 10" foam-board doghouses, dark-jointed red brick walls, cream plank roof with barge boards and ridge cap, arched door with flat cream trim and threshold, raised cream paw on the gable
look: Red plank/brick doghouse with a cream-wood shingled roof, arched doorway with cream trim, big cream paw print on the front gable. Currently DIY; a bought one is fine if it matches.
notes: Built at the board's scale: its doghouse is about as tall as the dog beside it (10-15"). Each weighs about 160 g (about 350 sq in of 3/16" foam board, 50 g of paint, 4 glue sticks), so it sits upright on a sturdy inner branch, wired through the floor, like the board's, with the gold loop as a safety tie.
how: Print pages 1, 2 and 8 at Actual size (check the 1" square). Cut on the flattened moving box with a fresh blade against the steel ruler; mark in pencil, never pen. Test the glue gun on an offcut first and glue onto the paper faces, not the bare foam edge (the hot gun melts the foam core). (1) Cut, per house, following the page-2 cut plan (boards 1-9 hold all six houses; board 10 is spare; measure each board first and if it is under 16" trim the difference off the roof overhang): front with the arched door (keep the door piece), back, two sides, two roofs, floor (page 2), four corner trims (page 2), and from page 8 the flat U-shaped arch trim (cut as one piece), two barge boards (flip one), the threshold and two ridge caps. Cut the 2.5" gable paw (pad + 4 toes, page 8) from the door piece. (2) Score while the template is still taped on: press the grey brick lines (page 1: courses about 0.9", bricks 1.5", staggered) and the roof board lines (page 2: every 1.25" parallel to the eave, joints every 1.5") through the paper with the empty ballpoint. Score the two plank lines on the threshold. (3) Paint flat, before assembly: the inside faces of the walls and the undersides of both roofs burnt sienna (stops the foam board warping; dark through the door); the roof tops, trims, threshold and paw one coat of cream (cream = 1/2 cup (120 ml) gesso + 1 tsp deep ochre + a pea-sized dab of burnt sienna; mix one batch for all six houses in a lidded cup and stir with a wood stick). (4) Assemble with hot glue: the walls round the floor (the floor sits inside the walls), then a toothpick across the inside of the two gable peaks with a 60 cm gold cord tied round it, the doubled loop coming out at the ridge, then the two roofs (3/4" overhang all round) either side of the cord. Poke two holes through the floor 2" apart with a toothpick. (5) Walls: brush the outside dark brick (dark brick = Crimson + Lamp Black about 10:1) and let it dry, then sponge-dab barn red = Naphthol Red + Crimson 1:1 over the brick faces only, twice, so the scored joints stay dark like the board's. (6) Second cream coat on the roof, trims, threshold and paw; dry-brush a little sienna along the roof boards for grain. Paint the ridge caps barn red with a touch of sienna. (7) Trims: glue the four corner trims on the wall corners, the threshold flat at the foot of the door (back edge against the wall, top level with the floor, sticking out 3/4"), the U arch trim round the door with its legs standing on the threshold, the barge boards along the two front roof edges meeting at the peak, the ridge caps as a peak over the ridge either side of the cord, and the five paw pieces on the front gable centred 2.84" below the peak (dotted on page 1). Darken the inside of the door opening with a little Lamp Black. (8) Hang: push a 10" floral wire through each floor hole, sit the house upright on a sturdy inner branch near the trunk and twist the wires round the branch; tie the gold loop to the branch above as a safety tie. About 40 min each once cut.
tools: Pencil and an empty ballpoint pen (office)

name: Paw ornaments (makes 10): Faylapa 6" bamboo hoops (16-pk) painted gold, tea-stained Aida face, black glitter paw, felt back, velvet bow
tools: Black tea bags, a kettle and a bowl (office kitchen)
notes: The same ornament with Amazon hoops: 6" bamboo with a brass screw, 16 in the pack (6 spare), $29.99 against $65.89 for eleven DeSerres hoops, and here Nov 20 instead of with the DeSerres parcel (Nov 25-27), so the hoops can be primed first. Only 3 packs were left on Nov 16 (Amazon-shipped, sold by HLSG, 4.6 stars from 42): order it first. If it sells out, choose the DeSerres-hoop option.
how: Per ornament (template pages 3 and 9). (1) Hoop: paint the outer ring only. Prime its outside face and front edge with gesso, then 2 coats of gold; leave the inner ring, the outer ring's inside face and the brass screw bare (paint there makes the clamp too tight and scuffs off). Paint one spare hoop with them. Cure 24 h. (2) Face: cut the Aida into 9 x 9" pieces (4 per sheet, 2 spare). Tea-stain them: 4 black tea bags in 1 L of just-boiled water for 10 min, soak the pieces 10 min, rinse once and dry flat under a towel (no tea: 1/4 tsp deep ochre and a drop of burnt sienna in 1 cup of water). Stain an offcut strip first and let it dry to check: it should be the board's warm biscuit-cream, not white. (3) Hoop it: lay a piece over the inner ring, press the outer ring down with the screw at the top, pull the edges evenly all round until drum-tight and tighten the screw. On the back trim the Aida to 1/2" outside the ring and hot-glue that margin to the inside of the inner ring. (4) Paw: cut a 3.6" paw (pad + 4 toes, page 3) from the black glitter cardstock and glue it to the centre with fabric glue. (5) Back: trace a 6" circle (page 9) on black felt with the white fabric marker, cut it out and hot-glue it to the back edge of the inner ring over the trimmed Aida, so the ornament is finished from behind. (6) Bow and hanger: tie a 9" bow from 37" of the velvet (two 4.5" loops, 8" tails, V-notched), wire it just above the screw with 8" of floral wire, and tie a 25 cm gold cord loop through the screw to hang it; twist the wire ends round the branch.

name: Bone ornaments (makes 8): 9" puffy biscuit bones of air-dry foam clay over a foil core, painted biscuit, sealed, hung level from two gold cords
look: Cream/biscuit-coloured 3D dog-bone ornament, about 4-5 in long, matte. Currently DIY; a bought one is fine if it matches.
notes: The board's bones are about as long as the dog is tall (7-11"), chunky like a biscuit (shaft about 0.27 of the length, knob span about 0.53), and hang level from two gold cords. Each takes about 117 g of wet foam clay over a foil core and weighs about 100 g dry.
how: Per bone (template page 4: 9" long, knob span 4.8", shaft 2.4", about 1" thick). Start the day the clay lands: only the painting waits for the DeSerres parcel. (1) Core: scrunch a 12 x 18" sheet of foil into a flat bone about 1/2" thick and 1/4" inside the page-4 outline all round, with a firm ball in each of the four knobs. Wire anchors: twist a small loop at one end of a 4" piece of floral wire and wrap its tail tightly round the foil inside each of the two upper knobs, with the loop just under the surface at the red marks. (2) Clay: on a piece of the drop sheet, lay two pencils 5" apart as 1/4" thickness guides (or two of the 6 mm wood sticks once DeSerres arrives) and press about 120 g of foam clay between them into a 1/4" sheet with a flat flap cut from the XL moving box. Wrap the core, smooth the seams with a damp finger and shape four round knobs and a flat-faced shaft against the page-4 outline. Dry 48 h, turning once. (3) Paint: 2 coats of the biscuit mix (1/2 cup gesso + 2 tsp deep ochre + 1 tsp burnt sienna); dry-brush burnt sienna on the edges and knobs; 1 coat of Mod Podge. (4) Hang with two cords, level, like the board: drill a hole about 3/4" deep at each red mark by twisting a toothpick down to the wire anchor. Cut a 50 cm gold cord, knot each end twice, fill each hole with hot glue and push one knotted end into each, so the glue grips the anchor. The two cords rise from the upper knobs and the bone hangs level; hang it from the middle of the cord and wire the cord to the branch with 8" of floral wire.

name: Shatterproof baubles, red & gold (100-pc set: 32 x 2.4", 36 x 1.6", 32 x 1.2")
viz: Red, green and gold baubles all over the tree

notes: Red and gold only (the board's fill is mostly red and gold); the forest green comes from the two 4" green glitter packs. About a third of the set is striped, diamond-painted or tartan-painted: hang those deep in the branches or leave them out, since the board's balls are plain. look: Large forest-green glitter baubles.

name: Large 3.15" champagne glitter baubles (12-pc)
look: Larger (3-4 in) champagne-gold glitter baubles.
notes: Old listing unavailable. New: champagne glitter 3.15" balls with sequin texture.

name: Mini knit stockings, red/green/cream, 4" (12-pk)
look: Mini pet stockings (5-7 in) in red tartan or red knit, ideally with a paw print or cream cuff. Not shown in the photo, listed in the bullet list.
notes: Cable-knit minis in red, forest green and cream with fluffy cuffs. Generic knit, so we add a small black felt paw to each cuff to make them pet stockings.
how: Trace 12 paws with the 1" template (page 3) on the black felt with the white fabric marker and cut them out. Glue one on each cream cuff: a dot of hot glue under the pad and toes, a bead of fabric glue round the edges. Wire each stocking to a branch through its loop with 6" of floral wire.

name: Red tartan fringed scarf, 12 x 66" (cut lengthwise into 3" strips: fringed scarves for 3 dogs and 3 cats)
look: Red tartan pet SCARVES with fringe (the dog and cat in the photo wear knit tartan scarves, not bandanas).
notes: Woven viscose/wool tartan, fringed on both short ends; the listing's body is 66" x 12" (167.6 x 30.5 cm), plus fringe. Six pets wear one: 3 goldens (2 on the tree, 1 under it) and 3 Miyoni tabbies (2 on the tree, 1 under it). Ships from and sold by Amazon US (cross-border), $35.28, free delivery Nov 19.
form_name: Tartan scarf for the pet scarves
how: (1) Lay the scarf flat and cut it lengthwise into four 3"-wide strips with sharp scissors, following a straight line of the tartan pattern (mark it in pencil if the pattern does not fall at 3"). (2) From each of strips 1-3, cut a 36" dog scarf from one fringed end and a 22" cat scarf from the other fringed end (8" left over); strip 4 is spare. (3) On each bare cut end, pull out the cross threads for 1.25" with a toothpick so it gets the same fringe as the factory end. Run a thin bead of fabric glue across the scarf just above each new fringe and along both long cut edges; dry 24 h. (4) Tie once round the neck at the side with both fringed ends hanging in front, over the wire.

name: Tartan ribbon cascades (makes 5): 4" tartan from under the topper to the bottom branches, with poufs
notes: The board's tartan runs from the topper to the bottom branches in loose poufs, with the big bows sitting on it. Five cascades, evenly round the tree, so the back is decorated too.
how: (1) Cut five 118" lengths of the 4" tartan (rolls 1 and 2 of the cut plan under the big bows). V-notch one end of each and seal it with a thin bead of fabric glue. (2) Space them evenly round the tree, about 72 degrees apart. Tuck the square end under the topper bow, about 8" below the tip, and wire it to the top stem with 6" of floral wire. (3) Work down and slightly round the tree: let the ribbon lie over the branch tips for about 12", then pinch it up into a pouf about 3" proud (about 8" of ribbon) and wire the pinch to a branch with 6" of floral wire. Make 4 poufs per cascade, about 10 ties in all, and finish at the bottom branches about 12" off the floor with the notched tail hanging free. (4) Wire 2-3 of the big tartan bows onto each cascade at a pouf, as on the board.

name: Big tartan bows, 11" with 15" tails (hand-tied from the 4" tartan, one loop each side)
notes: Hand-tied from our own tartan, so every bow matches the cascades. One loop each side, as on the board.
look: Large tartan bows with long tails.
how: Cut plan for the five 10-yd tartan rolls: roll 1 = three 118" cascades; roll 2 = two cascades, one 65" bow length and the 40" band for gift D; rolls 3-5 = five 65" bow lengths each (16 bows: 14 for the tree, 1 on top of gift D, 1 spare). Each bow: from a 65" (1.8 yd) length, cut a 6" knot piece. Leave a 15" tail, make one 5" loop to the left (about 11" of ribbon) and one to the right, pinch the centre with a 12" piece of floral wire, wrap the knot piece round the pinch and hot-glue it at the back, and leave a second 15" tail. V-notch both tails and run a thin bead of fabric glue along each notch. Twist the wire ends round a cascade pouf or a branch.

name: Velvet bows for the tree, 9" with 8" tails (hand-tied from the 1.5" dark red velvet)
notes: The board mixes solid deep red velvet bows with the tartan ones on the tree. Tied from the velvet roll we already buy, so they cost nothing extra.
how: Each bow: 37" of the 1.5" velvet: two 4.5" loops and 8" tails with V-notches, pinched with a 12" floral wire (as the paw-ornament bows). Wire them between the tartan bows, mostly on the right side and lower half like the board.

name: Dark red wired velvet ribbon, 1.5" x 25 yd (bows on the paw ornaments, the tree and the jar)
look: Deep red wired velvet, hand-tied.
notes: The board mixes solid deep red velvet bows with the tartan on the tree, and its paw-ornament and jar bows are the same velvet with soft loops and long tails. MEEDEE "dark red" is that colour; hand-tied, a 9" bow uses about 1 yd. Ships from and sold by Amazon US (cross-border; 4.6 stars from 1,350): check the checkout for an import-fee line.
form_name: Dark red velvet ribbon, 1.5" x 25 yd

name: Red/green/black tartan wired ribbon, 4" x 10 yd
look: Wired red tartan ribbon (red base with dark green and navy bands, thin gold/white lines), about 2.5 in wide, cascading down the tree.
notes: 4" wired tartan: the board's red-and-green plaid with a thin gold line. Cascades, hand-tied bows and the paw-paper gift's ribbon. name: Pine cone, holly & red berry evergreen picks (24-pk)

look: Glossy red holly-berry clusters.

look: Supply only.

name: Packing tape, Scotch tape 3-pk & plastic drop sheet (Canadian Tire)
notes: Pick up at Canadian Tire Edmonton South (2110 101 St NW) with the moving boxes. Scotch Magic Tape is $4.99 on sale until Nov 18 ($7.49 after); the plan counts $7.49.

name: Wrapped gifts (makes 4): moving boxes in tartan and kraft paw paper, cream burlap ribbon and bows, a tartan band and bow on the kraft box
look: Display gift boxes under the tree: kraft boxes with cream/burlap bows.
notes: Like the board: tartan boxes tied with cream ribbon and cream bows, and a kraft paw-print box with a tartan band and bow and a cream band with its own bow. Four bought boxes of known size, so paper and ribbon are calculated.
how: Boxes: A = small (18 x 11 x 12") as is, B = medium (16") as is, C = medium cut to 10" tall, D = small cut to 7" tall. (1) Fold and packing-tape the top flaps of all four shut. For C and D, mark the new height up from the open bottom on each corner, rule a pencil line round the box and cut the walls down along it with the art knife against the ruler, on the cutting box. The open bottom sits on the floor, hidden. (2) Tartan paper on A, B and C: cut two lengths of the box's girth (A 48", B 66", C 54") from the 17" roll and Magic-Tape them edge to edge on the back (1/2" overlap). Wrap so this join runs round the middle of the box, where the cream ribbon will cover it, with the girth overlap underneath; fold the ends like a parcel and tape (B's ends overlap only about 3/4": tape them well). (3) Kraft paw paper on D: two 17 x 40" sheets taped side by side, wrapped the same way with the join under the tartan band. (4) Ribbon: 1.5" cream burlap both ways round A, B and C, crossing on top over the paper join, ends taped underneath. On D, a 40" tartan band round the girth over the join and a 62" cream burlap band round the four sides, ends taped at the back. (5) Bows: tie a 10" cream burlap bow (40": two 5" loops, 6" tails, V-notched, pinched with 6" of floral wire) for each box and hot-glue it at the ribbon crossing (on D, on the front of the cream band). Tie one big tartan bow (as the tree bows) and hot-glue it on top of D at the tartan band.

name: Cream sherpa bone pillow, 15" (black felt paw added)
look: Large cream sherpa/fleece bone-shaped plush with a black paw print on the front.
notes: Curly cream sherpa bone like the big pillow under the board's tree; glue on a black felt paw. Shipped by Amazon from outside Canada (import fees deposit included), $6.11 delivery Nov 24. If it slips, buy a cream bone pillow at Homes Alive Pets South Edmonton on the gift-card trip.
how: It arrives vacuum-packed: unroll it 2-3 days before decorating so it fluffs up. Trace the 4.5" paw (template page 3) on the black felt with the white fabric marker and cut it out. Part the curly pile, put a dot of hot glue under the pad and each toe and press 30 s, then run a thin bead of fabric glue round the edges; dry flat.

notes: Old roll was green with tan check. New: red tartan with green & white lines, like the boxes in the photo.

name: Natural wicker gift basket with handle, 13" x 10.5" x 6" (remove the lace liner)
look: Natural honey-coloured wicker basket with a handle.
notes: Light natural willow like the board's honey wicker basket. It comes with a tie-in cream eyelet liner with a lace edge: untie and remove it (or swap in an offcut of the tartan scarf) so the basket reads as bare wicker, as on the board. 11" tall to the handle.
how: Untie and remove the lace liner. Wire the jar (to the handle), the bone toy, the rope and the ball in with 12" floral wires through the wicker. name: Faux dog biscuits (makes 64): foam clay cut with the 2.7" bone cutter, painted tan, sealed; set ring by ring against the glass of the jar
notes: The board's biscuits are small and tan in a 7" jar, so we cut them with the smallest bone cutter (2.7"), not the 3". 7 per ring x 7 rings line the glass, plus 12 on top: 61; we make 64. Inedible, so they last until the 2027 auction.
look: Biscuit-coloured bone treats filling the glass jar.
how: (1) Biscuits: on a piece of the drop sheet, press foam clay into a 1/4" sheet between two 6 mm wood sticks with a foam-board offcut, cut 64 bones with the 2.7" cutter (no cutter yet? trace the 3" outline on page 4 and cut with the knife), poke 3 dots in each with a toothpick and dry 24 h flat, turning once. Paint 2 coats of the tan mix (1/4 cup gesso + 2 tsp deep ochre + 1 tsp burnt sienna), then 1 coat of Mod Podge. (2) Jar, ring by ring: stand 7 biscuits flat against the glass (long side level, face out), stuff crumpled kraft paw paper (3 spare sheets, brown side out) behind them until they press on the glass, and repeat for 7 rings up to the shoulder; pile the last 12 on top. Nudge them into place through the mouth with a wood stick. (3) Wrap a 22" velvet band round the shoulder and hot-glue it at the back, tie a bow over the seam (44": two 5" loops, 9" tails), and fix the lid with 3 dots of hot glue (peels off later).
tools: A foam-board offcut (on the list) to press the clay
